needs.what: rule 115.3: the same player or object may be chosen once for each instance of the word "target" on a spell, so Rush of Dread's three "target opponent" modes may all name one opponent; enumerate_target_tuples has to let separate specs of one spell share a ref (while one spec's own count still needs distinct choices)
needs.why_existing_wont_do: targeting.enumerate_target_tuples drops any tuple in which two specs pick the same ref ("the same object cannot fill two targets"), so with spree_mode targets t1/t2/t3 every subset of two or more modes needs two or three different opponents: in a two-player game only single-mode casts exist, and at a pod each bought mode is forced onto a different opponent -- a different card. One shared spec is no fix: each mode's target opponent is chosen independently
